title: Surjective closed immersions: module equivalence and finite local models
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $h:T\hookrightarrow Y$ a surjective closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Work on either the small étale or the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with compatible universes and ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves $A_Y,A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Inverse image $h^*=h^{-1}$ uses the canonical identification $h^{-1}A_Y\cong A_T$, and $h_*$ has its induced $A_Y$-action [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The actual adjunction unit and counit are natural isomorphisms
$$H\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*h^*H,\qquad h^*h_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}N$$
for every module sheaf $H$ on $Y$ and $N$ on $T$. Thus $h^*$ and $h_*$ are quasi-inverse equivalences of module-sheaf categories. For every $A$-module $M$, $h^*\underline M_Y\cong\underline M_T$. A module sheaf $H$ on $Y$ is finite locally constant if and only if $h^*H$ is: here this means that on a covering family of the indicated site it is isomorphic to constant module sheaves with finite $A$-module models [def-constructible-locally-constant, def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. The same equivalence holds with the additional requirement that every local model be a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module. No Noetherianity or uniform nilpotence bound is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AB (lemma-thickening); lifting to constant-ring module objects and reflection of finite local models. Étale counterpart: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04DZ (theorem-topological-invariance). The module and finite-model clauses are extracted obligations, not literal assertions of the set-topos theorem.

proof.text: Etale clause proved: a surjective closed immersion is a universal homeomorphism. Apply the existing isEquivalence_upperStar and isEquivalence_lowerStar directly with coefficient category ModuleCat A. The actual adjunction unit and counit are then isomorphisms. The pro-etale clause remains to formalize: apply pro-etale topological invariance to the actual set-sheaf adjunction, also after each base change. Neither clause uses Noetherianity or a uniform nilpotence bound.

Remaining pro-etale argument: constant-coefficient inverse image identifies the module unit with the abelian unit, and finite-product adjunction lifting identifies that with the set unit. The pro-etale constant-ring map gives the canonical coefficient identification, and the ringed-topos module adjunction gives its actual direct-image action. The underlying unit is invertible by step 1; its inverse is linear by applying the inverse to the linearity identities. This applies after each base change. The etale proof uses the direct ModuleCat-valued equivalence instead.

Remaining pro-etale argument: The module direct image reflects isomorphisms: its underlying set functor is the equivalence in step 1, and an underlying inverse to a linear map is linear by step 2. For $N$ on $T$, the adjunction triangle says $h_*\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{h_*N}=1$. Since $\eta_{h_*N}$ is invertible, $h_*\varepsilon_N$ is invertible. Reflection gives that the actual counit $\varepsilon_N:h^*h_*N\to N$ is invertible. The unit and counit are natural by their adjunction, so the stipulated functors, with these actual maps, are quasi-inverse equivalences. In particular $h^*$ is fully faithful, as is each $h_V^*$.

source.place: Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), adjunction triangles and elementary inversion of linear maps

proof.text: Etale clause proved: apply upperStarConstantSheafIso objectwise. Remaining pro-etale argument: Apply the geometric inverse-image constant-module lemma with $R=A$ to the induced geometric morphism for any scheme morphism $f:U\to V$ on either indicated site. The canonical coefficient identification and actual module inverse image agree with those used here by step 2 (applied to $f$). The cited statement supplies the canonical $A_U$-linear isomorphism $f^*\underline M_V\cong\underline M_U$, natural in every $A$-linear map of models, for arbitrary $A$-modules $M$. In particular this proves the required comparison for $h$ and all morphisms between site objects and base changes used in steps 5–7; no finiteness of $M$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), as in the cited existing geometric constant-module comparison lemma

proof.text: Etale clause proved: the localized etale-site equivalence and its constant-sheaf comparison identify a local isomorphism with model M with a scheme-site inverse-image isomorphism with the same M. Pull back the trivializing cover. Use upperStarComp and pullback.condition to compare the two iterated inverse images, then pull back its chosen isomorphism and compose with upperStarConstantSheafIso. Convert back to the localized site. Reuse each finiteness proof and every finite-free splitting. Remaining pro-etale argument: base change preserves weakly etale arrows and fpqc coverings, inverse image along a site object is localized restriction, and constant-coefficient inverse image commutes with composition and restriction; the constant-module comparison retains each model.

source.place: lemma-pullback-locally-constant; sites.tex Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), localized inverse images

proof.text: Etale reflection proved in Lean: lift each member of a trivializing cover on T through h.Etale.objPreimage and objObjPreimageIso. The lifted objects cover Y: lift a point y to T by surjectivity of h, lift it to an original cover member, apply the inverse site-object isomorphism, and project the resulting point of the fiber product to the lifted object over Y. Pull back its given model isomorphism along the site-object isomorphism. upperStarComp and the cartesian-square identity identify its source with the base-changed pullback of H. Identify its target by upperStarConstantSheafIso. The first projection is a base-changed universal homeomorphism, so its ModuleCat-valued inverse image is fully faithful; preimageIso descends the model isomorphism. Convert back to the localized-site presentation. All models and splitting maps remain exactly the same.

source.place: Tag 04DZ (theorem-topological-invariance), Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance); lifting module trivializations by full faithfulness

proof.text: Remaining pro-etale argument: For reflection on the pro-étale site, let $C=\{U_a\to T\}$ trivialize $h^*H$ with models $M_a$. Apply the surjective-closed-cover-refinement theorem: it supplies a cover $B=\{V_b\to Y\}$ and, for each $b$, an index $a$ and a cartesian square $W_b=T\times_YV_b$, with maps $q_b:W_b\to V_b$, $p_b:W_b\to T$, and $r_b:W_b\to U_a$ over $T$. Here $q_b$ is the base change of $h$, so step 1 applies to it. Both $W_b\to T$ and $U_a\to T$ are site objects, and the between-objects lemma makes $r_b$ weakly étale. Inverse image along a pro-étale site object is localized restriction by the object-restriction theorem. Pull back the chosen trivialization along $r_b$. Compatibility with composition and restriction identifies its left side with $q_b^*(H|_{V_b})$, because the two composites $W_b\to Y$ agree in the square; step 4 identifies its right side with $\underline{M_a}_{W_b}$. Also $q_b^*\underline{M_a}_{V_b}\cong\underline{M_a}_{W_b}$. Lift this isomorphism and its inverse through the fully faithful $q_b^*$ of step 3. As in step 6 the lifted composites are identities, yielding $H|_{V_b}\cong\underline{M_a}_{V_b}$. Since $B$ is a cover this is the required pro-étale trivializing datum. It requires only refinement of $C$, not lifting every weakly étale object of $T$ to $Y$.

source.place: Tags 09AB (lemma-thickening), 09BK (lemma-closed-immersion-affines); covering refinement as stated in the cited existing node; localized module restrictions

proof.text: Proved for the etale clause; the same argument is planned for the remaining pro-etale clause: In steps 5–7 the scalar model is always the very same $A$-module as before pullback or descent, merely reindexed by a refined cover. Thus if the models are finite, they remain finite, and if each is a direct summand of some $A^n$, the same splitting maps and the same $n$ certify that property after either direction. This proves both local-model equivalences. The empty schemes cause no exception: a surjective closed immersion has empty source exactly when its target is empty; an empty covering is allowed and the local conditions are vacuous. The zero ring and zero module are also included throughout; no cancellation, nonzero element, or positive rank was used.

I read the unit sk-lem-sf-flat-model and how the parent det-sf-flat-model-generation uses the item in clause (2). Sources read: Stacks 09AB (proetale.tex l.4962) and 04DZ (etale-cohomology.tex l.6354). The statement is unchanged and true: a surjective closed immersion is integral, universally injective and surjective. I tested it on id, Spec k→Spec k[ε], a nil but not nilpotent ideal, the empty scheme, the zero ring and the zero module. Step checks: (1) universal homeomorphism and base change, with étale and pro-étale invariance for the actual unit and counit. (2) The module unit equals the abelian unit (lem-pe), which equals the set unit (adjunction-lifting lemma); the coefficient maps are canonical. (3) The counit follows from the triangle identity and reflection of isomorphisms. (4) lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module states exactly the constant-module comparison used. (5) The graph pair is initial, so the colimit is H(W); pro-étale restriction uses the object-restriction lemma; covers are preserved by base change (fpqc for pro-étale). (6) and (7) Reflection works by lifting covers, or by the Lean cover-refinement node with r_b weakly étale, plus full faithfulness of the base-changed pullback. (8) The models are literally unchanged. The declared tool_uses are acceptable; the other off-unit citations are Mathlib leaves or closed in slopmaster2. No cycle, no new nodes, no duplicate: lemma-constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance and the condensed nodes are narrower or about different coefficients. Batch-5 check on lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance: it is Stacks 09AB, a general pro-étale topological-invariance result. Neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives it. Its full closure (1146 nodes) contains no other sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality node, no batch-4 target and no nt-assume leaf. The item's pro-étale clauses genuinely need it, so I accept the citation as outside the assumed statements. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem sfbEtale_surjectiveClosed_module_invariance {T Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion h] [Surjective h] (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] : IsIso (Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).unit ∧ IsIso (Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).counit ∧ (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).IsEquivalence ∧ (Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).IsEquivalence ∧ (∀ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} A, Nonempty ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).obj ((constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj M) ≅ (constantSheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj M)) ∧ (∀ (H : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (projective : Bool), sfbEtaleFiniteLocalModels A H projective ↔ sfbEtaleFiniteLocalModels A ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).obj H) projective)
lean.note: Two theorem statements cover the etale and pro-etale clauses. The etale version uses the published fixed ModuleCat-valued presentation; the pro-etale version uses the recorded ordinary constant-ring module operations, with their actual normalized adjunction. The two finite-local-model helpers expand the local-model clauses of this node using existing localized constant sheaves; the Bool selects whether explicit finite-free retractions are required. No stalk-based replacement, etale-origin condition, Noetherian assumption, or uniform nilpotence bound.
